extracted.intended_audience: educated readers of 18th-century political/economic pamphlets; commentators and critics of public finance and foreign policy
extracted.subtask_description: A close critical appraisal of another writer's pamphlet on war, peace, and public finance, focusing on the soundness of arguments, empirical evidence, accounting, and the practical consequences of policy. The page enumerates what a good peace should secure and gives standards for rigorous argumentation about finance and trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requisites of a good peace
rubrics_metrics.description: I apprehend they may be reduced to these: 1. Stability; 2. Indemnification; 3. Alliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good peace must secure (1) stability of settlement (so it will last), (2) adequate compensation/indemnification (to offset the costs of war), and (3) alliances or diplomatic arrangements that prevent future conspiracies or leagues; the negotiation should aim to produce tangible security on these three heads rather than mere assertions of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show that enemies had money upon better terms
rubrics_metrics.description: To bring them home to his purpose, he ought to have shown that our enemies had money upon better terms; which he has not shown, neither can he.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When arguing that an opponent was financially advantaged, provide evidence that they could raise funds on more favorable terms (rates, maturities, sources). Mere assertion that the enemy had cheaper money is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate that money they raised procured a more lucrative return
rubrics_metrics.description: He ought to have shown that the money they raised, upon whatever terms, had procured them a more lucrative return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claiming that an opponent's financing produced superior outcomes, trace how the funds translated into commerce, conquest, or other profitable returns; show the causal link between financing terms and material gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of principles and internal coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: This author soon grows weary of his principles. They seldom last him for two pages together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments should be consistent across the work—do not adopt positions in one passage that contradict claims elsewhere (e.g., dismissing the value of conquest but elsewhere basing security on the chance of conquering colonies). Maintain coherent principles throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult public experience and commanders before asserting certainty of conquest
rubrics_metrics.description: It were better that he had examined a little what advantage the peace gave us towards the invasion of these colonies, which we did not possess before the peace. It would not have been amiss if he had consulted the public experience, and our commanders, concerning the absolute certainty of those conquests on which he is pleased to found our security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims of military or imperial certainty must be grounded in practical, empirical advice—consult experienced commanders and records of past operations rather than asserting that possession or conquest is 'certain' or 'easy.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare like with like; include corresponding articles when comparing expenditures
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to render the articles which compose the peace establishment in the two periods correspondent (for otherwise they cannot be compared), we must deduct first, his articles of the deficiency of land and malt... We must also deduct the deficiencies of funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing financial totals across periods, ensure the component items correspond exactly; include or exclude the same categories in both periods, and adjust for items (deficiencies, extraordinaries) so as to avoid misleading comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid double-counting interest and deficiencies in public accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: To charge the interest in one part of the account, and then the deficiency in the other, would be charging 600,000_l._. The deficiency of funds must therefore be also deducted from the peace establishment in the 'Considerations'; and then the peace establishment... will be reduced...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not count the same burden twice (e.g., charging interest and also charging the deficiency of the sinking fund). Present a single, correct accounting of the annual charge by computing interest once and handling fund deficiencies consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish funded vs unfunded debt and only compute interest on items that carry interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Of this long list of nine articles, only two, the exchequer bills, and part of the navy debt, carried any interest at all... The whole navy debt indeed amounted to 4,576,915_l._; but of this only a part carried interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When estimating annual interest burdens, identify which components of the principal actually carry interest. Do not apply a uniform interest rate to an aggregate that includes non‑interest-bearing items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assert numerical claims without providing proof or primary-source references
rubrics_metrics.description: This he has done in his usual manner, by assertion, without troubling himself either with proof or probability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Back numerical statements with citations (journals of the House of Commons, registers, prior authoritative works). Unsupported assertions of sums or differences are unreliable and invite refutation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use contemporary records and averages to test claims about trade and consumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the revenue on consumption speak for itself... Average of net excise, since the new duties, three years ending 1767... Here is, on the contrary, an immense increase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess claims about manufacturing decline or revenue contraction by consulting excise returns, export totals, and multi‑year averages rather than relying on rhetorical lamentations. Provide concrete tables or averages to support conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for structural and regional changes in manufactures and trade
rubrics_metrics.description: A trade sometimes seems to perish when it only assumes a different form... some manufactures have decayed in the west and south, which have made new and more vigorous shoots when transplanted into the north... vast addition to the mass of British trade, which has been made by the improvement of Scotland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When diagnosing decline, consider shifts in product type, changes of location, and emergence of new manufacturing centres; apparent local decline can accompany national improvement in different forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of scare-tactics and rhetorical exaggeration; prefer sober analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: He raises by art magic a thick mist before our eyes, through which glare the most ghastly and horrible phantoms... Let us therefore calmly... appreciate those dreadful and deformed gorgons and hydras.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid building arguments around alarmist imagery or emotional horror; evaluate policy claims calmly and analytically, exposing 'phantoms' with empirical counter‑evidence rather than matching rhetorical excess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit the scope of customs-entry inaccuracy arguments to 'free goods' and certificate goods
rubrics_metrics.description: The inaccuracy of these entries can extend only to FREE GOODS... The article of CERTIFICATE GOODS re-exported, a vast branch of our commerce, admits of no error... The author therefore is not warranted from the known error in some of the entries, to make a general defalcation from the whole balance in our favor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When challenging export statistics, recognize that entry inaccuracies mainly affect free goods; goods with drawbacks/certificates are reliably recorded. Do not assume uniform overstatement across all export categories without examining which categories are affected.
